solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Primarily mumbled speaking? (9)

indicatorNotes.Primarily: primarily = first of all, so take the first letter

annotation.surface: A question about a way of talking that begins as a mumble.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: talk that opens with a mumble and carries on as speech is exactly the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: low, indistinct talk really is speaking in which mumbling comes first and foremost.

entries.clue: Bother with problem climbing plant (7)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards

blocks.note: drat! and bother! are both mild curses
a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: A gardener annoyed by trouble with a climbing plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' reads as one thing; 'climbing' is the instruction, turning DRAT + SUM upside down, and 'plant' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the condiment comes from the seeds of a cabbage-family plant of the same name.

entries.clue: Pundit snubbed new wave band (7,4)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: snubbed = cut short, like a snub nose, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the New York group fronted by David Byrne; its last letter is cut

annotation.surface: A commentator refusing to acknowledge an up-and-coming group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' looks like the pundit being rude; it means cut short. Talking Heads lose their final S.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: television slang for a commentator shown only from the shoulders up, giving opinions.

entries.clue: Local forgetting name boosted musical (5)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: forgetting the N leaves it out
indicatorNotes.boosted: in a down clue, boosted means pushed upwards, read bottom to top

blocks.note: a local is someone born there

annotation.surface: A resident who can't recall a title perks up at a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a pub, the usual crossword meaning; here it is a resident. NATIVE loses N, and ATIVE is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Lloyd Webber and Rice show about Eva Perón.

entries.clue: Remain popular, principally doing fine (7)

indicatorNotes.principally: principally = chiefly, first, so the first letter

annotation.surface: Advice on staying well liked while mostly doing well.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a literary verb, rare outside religious writing, which is why the wordplay is so plain.
annotation.definitionFit: Literary synonym: to dwell within, to abide, as the spirit is said to abide in a believer.

entries.clue: Prisoner’s turning 44? (3)

indicatorNotes.turning: turning round, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: an old lag is a convict

annotation.surface: A convict changing into whatever answer 44 turns out to be.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 44 down is DAMSEL. The question mark flags that the answer is only an informal example of one.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a young woman, the modern word for what 44 down calls her.

entries.clue: One evening, around 6 — having cancelled 9 — enlightenment (7)

indicatorNotes.around: the evening wraps around what follows
indicatorNotes.having cancelled: cancelling IX takes those letters out of SIX

blocks.note: nine in Roman numerals, cancelled from SIX

annotation.surface: A cryptic scheduling note that seems to point to other answers in the grid.
annotation.walkthrough: 6 and 9 look like cross-references to other clues; they are just numbers, one written as a word and one as a Roman numeral, so the subtraction leaves a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean a sudden clear understanding of something.

entries.clue: Northern jerk, in principle, just the same (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the northern jerk goes in the principle

annotation.surface: Calling a northerner an idiot on principle, all the same.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' tempts as an insult; it is a twitch, and the northern jerk goes in as one unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: exactly alike in every respect.

entries.clue: Compiler in The Sun? (6)

blocks.note: the sun goes down every evening, so it is one that sets

annotation.surface: Asking who writes the crossword in The Sun newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, so the surface asks about its crossword writer; the second sense makes the sun itself the thing that sets.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: a crossword compiler, and whimsically anything that sets, as the sun does each evening.

entries.clue: Pretend to search sewage? (2,7,3,7)

blocks.note: search = go through; motions are, medically, bowel movements

annotation.surface: A sewer inspector only faking the job.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'motions' in its medical sense, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something only for show, and literally rummaging through the sewage.

entries.clue: Combinations of cards must be a dodgy hand at poker? (7)

blocks.note: a count far too big: a pack holds only four of the next piece
the top cards in a poker hand

annotation.surface: A card sharp caught holding an impossible hand.
annotation.walkthrough: Ten aces would be a dodgy hand indeed. A tenace, in bridge and whist, is two high cards in one suit with a gap between, such as ace and queen.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term: in bridge, a holding of two cards separated by one missing rank.

entries.clue: Cleaned sheds quietly, and sulked (5)

indicatorNotes.sheds: sheds = casts off, so a letter is lost

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; one P is shed

annotation.surface: Someone who scrubbed out the garden sheds and felt sorry for themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like the thing cleaned; it is the verb, casting off one P.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean moping about in low spirits.

entries.clue: Pulse raised over American — Hayworth, perhaps — getting cocktail (9)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means read upwards
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over means placed above

blocks.note: gram is a pulse, as in chickpeas

annotation.surface: A heartbeat quickening over a Hollywood star as she orders a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is the edible seed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tequila, lime and orange-liqueur drink served in a salt-rimmed glass.

entries.clue: Start hoping Liberal makes hostile comment at last (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Liberal: liberal = free, loose, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A Liberal's new optimism ending in a snipe at a rival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the usual L for a party member; here it is the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a barbed remark made on leaving, from the Parthian archers who shot while retreating.

entries.clue: Dirt from underneath my mannequin (5)

indicatorNotes.from underneath: in a down clue, coming from underneath means read upwards

annotation.surface: Finding grime under a shop-window figure.
annotation.walkthrough: Coming 'from underneath' only makes sense as an instruction in a down clue, where the letters climb from the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a model figure used to display clothes.

entries.clue: Second charming and mostly boring chap is hedonistic (4-9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly = most of it, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A second suitor, charming but rather dull, who lives only for pleasure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second charming' reads as a description of a man; second is just S.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: both describe someone who gives in to their own pleasures.

entries.clue: Time machine that flies backwards — strange instrument (5,4)

indicatorNotes.backwards: the flying machine is written backwards
indicatorNotes.strange: rum is old slang for strange

blocks.note: a rum do is an odd business

annotation.surface: A time machine that travels in reverse, which would be a strange device.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time machine' reads as a unit from science fiction; time is only T, and the machine is the flying one. Rum = strange is British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a drum pitched between the snare and the bass, used in marching bands.

entries.clue: A contemptible person had to stir up trouble (7)

annotation.surface: A nasty piece of work who set out to cause trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' looks like an auxiliary verb in 'had to'; it is the meal sense, ate. A git is British slang for an unpleasant person.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to campaign or stir people up for a cause.

entries.clue: Aardvark can’t be arboreal for a stretch (7)

indicatorNotes.for a stretch: a stretch of the text, running across word boundaries, holds the letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of can’t, through be, into the start of arboreal

annotation.surface: An aardvark can't live in the trees, not even for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is zoologically true: the animal digs burrows rather than climbing.
annotation.definitionFit: Alternative name: the South African animal is also called an earth pig or antbear, after its diet.

entries.clue: Ailing businesses dig out good news, eventually (1,8,2,8)

indicatorNotes.out: out = in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Struggling firms digging up something to celebrate at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dig out' reads as a phrasal verb; 'dig' is fodder and 'out' is the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: something unwelcome at first that turns out well in the end.

entries.clue: Suspicious about sex aid (7)

indicatorNotes.about: the word for suspicious goes about the other

annotation.surface: Being wary of a sex toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sex aid' reads as one thing; sex is IT, and aid alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: help given freely to those in need.

entries.clue: Like Italian to punch timekeeper’s hands-free kit (7,5)

blocks.note: slang: I dig it = I like it
slang: to clock someone is to hit them

annotation.surface: An Italian who wants to hit the man with the stopwatch and his phone headset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hands-free kit' suggests a phone gadget; the joke is a timepiece without hands.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a clock showing numbers instead of hands is literally hands-free.

entries.clue: Arranged to meet and test stone head, off and on (7)

indicatorNotes.off and on: skip one letter, take one, skip one, take one

blocks.note: the abbreviation for the British weight of 14 pounds
h-E-a-D, the second and fourth letters

annotation.surface: Lovers who agree to meet, then test each other's resolve.
annotation.walkthrough: A tryst is a lovers' secret meeting; as a verb it means arranging one.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic verb: fixing a time and place for a rendezvous.

entries.clue: Glam rock band vocalist blocked by Liberal politician, say, making false accusations (10)

indicatorNotes.blocked by: the vocalist is blocked by L sitting inside

blocks.note: British 1970s glam band, famous for 'Tiger Feet'

annotation.surface: A pop singer's career blocked by a politician spreading lies.
annotation.walkthrough: Mud were a British glam rock band of the 1970s. 'Liberal politician' reads as a unit, but the politician belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: slinging mud is making smears; 'say' marks a politician as just one example.

entries.clue: Jockey possibly carrying unusual sign for spectator close to the action (9)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the jockey carries the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.unusual: unusual = out of the normal order

annotation.surface: A jockey holding a strange placard for the crowd near the track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' tempts as an anagram signal; here it is the rider, and 'unusual' does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: someone seated beside the boxing ring.

entries.clue: Periodically, driver steals fuel (6)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter

annotation.surface: A motorist who now and then siphons petrol.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' reads as how often the driver steals; it is the instruction to take every other letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: heavy oil burned in lorries and many cars.

entries.clue: Compassion encapsulates English faith (5)

indicatorNotes.encapsulates: to encapsulate is to enclose, so E goes inside

annotation.surface: Kindness containing a very English kind of belief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Encapsulates' is the verb doing the containing; the E goes one letter from the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: religious devotion.

entries.clue: Foretell welcoming a new preacher (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the verb welcomes the letters inside

annotation.surface: A prophet who warns that a new preacher is coming.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare word from the Latin for preaching, used of Dutch Reformed ministers.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare synonym: a preaching minister or friar.

entries.clue: He’s sinful, complex, and generous (9)

indicatorNotes.complex: complex = intricately put together, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A character sketch of a man who sins but is complicated and kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as describing the man; it is the anagram signal. The fodder turns sinful into its opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: putting others first.

entries.clue: Discover Harry near hut (7)

indicatorNotes.Harry: to harry is to harass, so the letters are knocked about

annotation.surface: Finding someone called Harry close to a shed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name; it is the verb, to harass.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to find, especially by digging.

entries.clue: Every individual jamming can debate etc. (5-2)

indicatorNotes.jamming: every individual is jammed into the can

annotation.surface: Everyone cramming into a room to argue about everything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an informal session of lectures and debate on a topical issue.

entries.clue: During riot, steal wheels before fight in storage area (7)

indicatorNotes.wheels: to wheel round is to turn about, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: looting is stealing in the chaos of a riot

annotation.surface: Rioters making off with car wheels before a brawl in a warehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' reads as stolen car parts; it is the turning instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose definition: a box in which tools are stored.

entries.clue: He backs end to receding layer of cells (11)

indicatorNotes.backs: backs = comes behind, so the He part goes last
indicatorNotes.receding: receding = going back, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol, expanded to the element's name

annotation.surface: A man putting an end to a thinning layer of cells.
annotation.walkthrough: He is read backwards from the usual abbreviation trick: the symbol gives the full name of the element, not the other way round.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term: the thin layer of cells lining blood vessels and the heart.

entries.clue: Dog running for food (6)

blocks.note: a machine that is on is running

annotation.surface: A dog chasing its dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running' reads as the dog's action; it means working, switched on.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the meat of a mature sheep.

entries.clue: Juvenile friends choose malts, shockingly (11)

indicatorNotes.shockingly: shockingly = in a shaken-up way, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Underage friends shockingly picking whiskies.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a scandal: youngsters picking out malt whiskies.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: friends made at school, so young ones.

entries.clue: Twist nasty article in Die Zeit (7)

blocks.note: a German definite article; Die Zeit is a German newspaper

annotation.surface: A spiteful slant given to a piece in a German newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece, which Die Zeit would print; it is the grammatical article, German for 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a winding bend, as in a river.

entries.clue: Old footballer is selected, yes? (6,5)

blocks.note: a player who is selected is in the side

annotation.surface: A veteran player checking he has been picked for the team.
annotation.walkthrough: The inside right was an attacking position in the old five-forward football formation, now gone, hence 'Old'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a player in a former football position.

entries.clue: Short distance from home, stopping volatile host having argument (6-5)

indicatorNotes.stopping: the home stops up the gap inside the host
indicatorNotes.volatile: volatile = unstable, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.having: having = with, so ROW is added

annotation.surface: A short-tempered host within walking distance, arguing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short distance from home' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'distance' and 'from' links.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: as far as a stone can be thrown, so very near.

entries.clue: Stupid and innocent type showered after taking ecstasy (11)

indicatorNotes.taking: to take a drug is to take it in, so the innocent type holds the ecstasy inside
indicatorNotes.after: after = later in time, so in the written answer the showered part comes later

annotation.surface: A naive dimwit taking a drug and then a shower.
annotation.walkthrough: The ecstasy sits between the M and B of the innocent lamb; E for the drug is standard slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: slow-witted.

entries.clue: Completely down with policeman arresting Republican (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.arresting: the policeman arrests R, holding it inside

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to down it

annotation.surface: A policeman arresting a Republican and knocking him fully down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as floored; it is the British slang verb to neck, to drink in one go.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: wholly, bodily, as when someone is thrown out neck and crop.

entries.clue: Get rid of a book from Poland missing page (7)

indicatorNotes.missing: missing = lacking, so P is dropped

annotation.surface: Throwing out a Polish book with a page gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From Poland' means Polish, and losing P turns it into a word ending.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to do away with entirely.

entries.clue: Enduring model: “I’ll be in bed, scratching head” (9)

indicatorNotes.model: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped
indicatorNotes.scratching head: scratching off its head, the first letter goes

blocks.note: BED without its first letter, also fodder

annotation.surface: A model's lazy promise to stay in bed, scratching her head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person speaking; it is the command to reshape the letters that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: impossible to remove, so lasting.

entries.clue: One bad apple overwhelms Irish public service broadcaster, I think? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase describing what the answer does

indicatorNotes.bad: bad = spoilt, so the letters of one are rearranged
indicatorNotes.overwhelms: the apple overwhelms the broadcaster, swallowing it

blocks.note: Cox's Orange Pippin, a British eating apple
Raidió Teilifís Éireann, Ireland's national broadcaster

annotation.surface: A rotten apple spoiling Ireland's national broadcaster, in someone's opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One bad apple' reads as a proverb; 'bad' mixes ONE and the apple is a Cox. 'I think?' is not a hedge but the definition: the brain part where thinking happens.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the outer layer of the brain, where higher thought such as 'I think' takes place.

entries.clue: Rank those people’s answer fills, not on TV (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.fills: the answer fills the word for those people's, sitting inside it

annotation.surface: An order to rank people's answers to a quiz that has been taken off television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a verb for putting in order; it is the adjective, foul-smelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: no longer being broadcast.

entries.clue: Whimsically remove my colour scheme (5)

blocks.note: the prefix de- means remove, as in de-ice; 'whimsically' admits the liberty
my! and cor! are both British exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: A mischievous instruction to get rid of the way a room has been painted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is the exclamation. The setter admits that taking remove as a prefix is a whimsical liberty.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a room's decorative scheme, colours included.

entries.clue: Feel exhilarated or irate, and strange (5,2,3)

indicatorNotes.strange: strange = odd, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A list of moods swinging from joy to anger to oddness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of feelings, so 'strange' seems one more mood rather than the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be so happy you seem to walk on air.

entries.clue: Asians, mostly quiet, recalled embracing father (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the whole reads in reverse

annotation.surface: A group of Asians, mostly quiet, remembering how they held their father.
annotation.walkthrough: PA goes inside SILEN, and the whole, SILAPEN, is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: people from Nepal, a South Asian country.

entries.clue: Radon for sale is silly, futile exercise (1,5,6)

indicatorNotes.silly: silly = scatterbrained, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Trying to sell a radioactive gas is a silly, pointless business.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sound: radon is a radioactive gas no one would buy, so selling it really would be pointless.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a task with no hope of success.

entries.clue: Some visas in Estonia result in Scottish land transfers (7)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters, so the answer is hidden inside

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of visas, through in, into the start of Estonia

annotation.surface: Visas granted in Estonia leading to property deals in Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: A sasine is the Scots-law term for taking legal possession of land; the answer is a rare word, so the hidden word makes it gettable.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional legal term: in Scots law, the act of giving possession of land.

entries.clue: Resentment, as underground cell gets diamonds for nationalists’ leader (7)

indicatorNotes.gets: the cell gets a new letter
indicatorNotes.for: for = in place of, so D replaces N

blocks.note: first letter of nationalists, coming out

annotation.surface: Nationalists' leader jailed underground, and resentful about the diamonds taken.
annotation.walkthrough: The swap works on DUNGEON's middle N; the first N in nationalists is what leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, mostly in the phrase 'in high dudgeon': angry resentment.

entries.clue: Young woman checks middle of eyelid (6)

indicatorNotes.middle of: the middle of a word is its centre, and with six letters that is the third and fourth

blocks.note: to dam is to hold back, check

annotation.surface: A young woman checking something in her eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like examining; it means holds back, as a dam checks water.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: a young unmarried woman, as in damsel in distress.

entries.clue: Reveal properties for hire next to border (3,4)

indicatorNotes.next to: the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: in Britain a let is a property rented out
an edge, as of a cup

annotation.surface: A landlord disclosing rental properties near the frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a let is a rented property, so properties for hire are lets.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to reveal something by accident.

entries.clue: Delicate predicament, having taken top off (5)

indicatorNotes.having taken top off: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which comes off

blocks.note: a sorry state; its top letter goes

annotation.surface: A tricky situation made worse by someone removing their top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delicate predicament' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Delicate'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: gentle, as in a light touch.

entries.clue: Genus of lichens lives on plot (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, on means placed after

blocks.note: to plot points is to graph them
to be is to live, exist

annotation.surface: A lichen growing on a patch of ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a patch of land, where lichen would live; it is a chart.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term: script lichens, named for their writing-like markings.

entries.clue: With two days to replace bishop, starts going back with bosses (7)

indicatorNotes.going back: going backwards, so the letters reverse
indicatorNotes.to replace: to replace is to take the place of, so the two days stand where the bishop was

annotation.surface: An office where two days off go to replace the bishop, and new starters answer to bosses.
annotation.walkthrough: DEBUTS reversed gives STUBED; DD then goes where the B was.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a boss is a round metal stud, so something studded has bosses.

entries.clue: Regularly rush, though? Yes (2-3)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether to hurry and getting a casual yes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' starts with the second letter here; the odd letters give nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a murmur of agreement.

entries.clue: Revolutionary’s rude, transfixed by reduced profit (9)

indicatorNotes.transfixed by: the reduced profit is pierced by the rude word, which sits inside
indicatorNotes.reduced: cut short, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A rebel sneering while his dwindling profits are pinned down.
annotation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight for Italian unification. The biscuit named after him is a British favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 19th-century Italian revolutionary general.

entries.clue: Start to suspect Mr Ed, say, is unrealistic candidate in election (8-5)

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: Mr Ed was the title animal of an American TV sitcom, who could speak

annotation.surface: Suspecting that a TV horse is standing for office without a hope.
annotation.walkthrough: A stalking horse stands in a leadership contest to test the waters for a stronger rival, with no real hope of winning.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a no-hope candidate put up to split the vote or test support.

entries.clue: Virtually make up Chinese language (3)

indicatorNotes.Virtually: virtually = almost, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read upwards

blocks.note: used as it stands, less its last letter

annotation.surface: Nearly inventing a language from China.
annotation.walkthrough: Kam, also called Dong, is a language of southern China.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the tongue of the Kam or Dong minority people.

entries.clue: Sweat damaged leather strap (5)

indicatorNotes.damaged: damaged = knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A strap of leather spoilt by perspiration.
annotation.walkthrough: A tawse is the Scottish schoolmaster's leather strap, used for punishment.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional term: the leather belt once used in Scottish schools to punish pupils.

entries.clue: Maybe McCartney and Starr’s final piece is outstanding (7)

blocks.note: the fashion designer, Paul McCartney's daughter

annotation.surface: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr's latest song is a triumph.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at the two Beatles; 'Maybe' says McCartney stands for a different McCartney.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: starlike, so exceptional.

entries.clue: Twisted young lady in Leeds, perhaps becoming half-hearted (9)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: half of the heart is taken: the middle PP becomes P

blocks.note: Yorkshire dialect for perhaps; one of its centre Ps goes

annotation.surface: A contorted girl in Leeds who is losing heart.
annotation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire, where Leeds is, 'happen' is used to mean perhaps. Its heart is PP, and half of that goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: deformed, out of shape.
